article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Autoflowering hybrid
Genetics: AK-47 × Ruderalis
Breeder: Pitt Bully
THC Content: 16–19%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet citrus, spice, earth, herbal notes
Flowering Time (Indoor): 40 days of flowering
Outdoor Harvest Time: 80 days from germination
Indoor Yield: 40 g per plant
Outdoor Yield: 40 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Cetme comes from an earlier generation of autoflowering cannabis, when breeders were still working to prove that automatic genetics could offer more than tiny plants and modest-quality weed. Developed by the Spanish breeder Pitt Bully, this compact cultivar took the celebrated AK-47 and introduced ruderalis genetics to create a plant that flowers according to age rather than changes in daylight. The unusual part was the breeding objective: instead of making the fastest autoflower possible, Pitt Bully accepted a somewhat longer development cycle in exchange for better production. Historical specifications put the complete run at roughly 80 days from germination, with THC around 16–19% and a predominantly sativa-style effect.
Genetics and Lineage

Cetme is essentially an autoflowering interpretation of AK-47. Pitt Bully crossed AK-47 with ruderalis-derived genetics, preserving much of the parent cultivar’s psychoactive character while introducing automatic flowering and a much smaller physical frame. That makes the pedigree comparatively straightforward at a time when many modern cannabis hybrids contain several generations of named polyhybrids.

The AK-47 side carries considerable genetic diversity of its own. Serious Seeds created the original cultivar in 1992 after working with Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan cannabis populations. The breeder describes AK-47 as approximately 65% sativa, with its Latin American and Southeast Asian ancestry contributing to the more cerebral side of the plant while Afghan genetics add physical depth, resin production, and compact flower formation.

Ruderalis serves a different purpose. Its importance is not primarily flavor or potency but flowering behavior. Cannabis ruderalis populations evolved in regions with relatively short growing seasons, and autoflowering occurs largely according to plant age rather than the photoperiod trigger used by conventional marijuana varieties. Pitt Bully used that characteristic to turn AK-47-derived genetics into a small plant capable of progressing from seed to harvest without a deliberate 12-hour flowering light cycle.
Effects and Experience

The breeder historically characterized Cetme as predominantly sativa in effect, despite the additional ruderalis and indica ancestry buried within its family tree. The experience tends to emphasize the mental side of cannabis rather than immediately producing a heavy, sleepy body sensation. An initial lift in mood can develop into a brighter, more engaged state that fits daytime activities better than the couch-bound reputation associated with many compact autoflowers.

AK-47 provides a useful reference point for understanding the experience, although Cetme should not be assumed to duplicate its parent exactly. Serious Seeds describes AK-47 as combining cerebral and physical qualities, with considerable potency despite relatively manageable growth. Cetme’s historical 16–19% THC range places it below many modern high-THC marijuana cultivars, but that does not make the plant weak. For consumers with low tolerance, THC at these concentrations can still create substantial intoxication.

As the high progresses, the initial mental energy can settle into a more comfortable hybrid calm. This transition helps separate the cultivar from extremely stimulating tropical sativas. Larger doses may increase physical relaxation while also amplifying changes in attention and perception. Dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, and anxious or racing thoughts remain possible THC-related effects, particularly when more weed is consumed before the first dose has fully developed.
Medical Benefits

There are no controlled clinical trials examining Cetme as an individual medical marijuana cultivar. For that reason, claims that this specific strain treats depression, fatigue, anxiety, pain, or another condition should be viewed as anecdotal rather than established medical evidence. A strain name does not guarantee a consistent chemical composition across different plants and harvests.

Cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly have received considerably more research. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health reports evidence suggesting modest benefits for certain forms of chronic pain, while cannabinoid medicines have recognized applications for chemotherapy-associated nausea and vomiting. Evidence for many other commonly advertised cannabis uses remains limited, mixed, or still developing.

Cetme’s relatively upbeat character may appeal to some medical cannabis consumers who want to avoid strong daytime sedation, but stimulation can also be counterproductive for people who are sensitive to THC. Actual cannabinoid testing of the flower being consumed is more informative than assuming every Cetme plant contains exactly the historical 16–19% THC figure.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Cetme is a difficult strain to describe responsibly from a terpene standpoint because Pitt Bully did not leave behind a verified laboratory terpene panel or detailed official tasting profile. Rather than assigning fashionable terpene percentages that cannot be substantiated, its aromatic character is best interpreted cautiously through its dominant AK-47 heritage.

The original AK-47 has a sweet and spicy foundation with citrus notes, according to Serious Seeds. Mature flowers can also display fruity, earthy, and mildly woody qualities depending on the individual plant and growing environment. In Cetme, those characteristics may appear in a lighter form, with sweet citrus and dry spice sitting over a greener herbal background.

That comparatively traditional profile fits the strain’s age. This is not cannabis bred around candy, pastry, artificial fruit, or heavy dessert aromas. Properly dried flower is better expected to occupy the classic spectrum of citrus, herbs, earth, spice, and subtle sweetness. Phenotype variation, nutrition, temperature, harvest timing, and curing can all alter those impressions considerably.
Growing Information

Compact size is one of Cetme’s most practical features. Historical Pitt Bully specifications place mature plants around 50 centimeters, or roughly 20 inches, making this weed particularly suitable for limited vertical space. Unlike photoperiod cannabis, the plant begins flowering according to its developmental clock, so there is little opportunity to compensate later for problems that slow early vegetative growth.

The original breeder recommendations were unusually specific about the root zone. Cetme was intended to be planted directly into its finishing container rather than repeatedly transplanted, with Pitt Bully historically recommending relatively modest containers of approximately 4–7 liters. The breeder also warned against excessive watering during the early phase. Once plants had established themselves and entered vigorous flowering, they could tolerate more conventional irrigation and feeding.

Timing is roughly divided between about 40 days of vegetative and transitional development and another 40 days associated with flowering, giving approximately 80 days from germination to outdoor harvest. Historical production was listed around 40 grams per plant. Those numbers place Cetme firmly in the compact early-autoflower category rather than beside today’s large automatic cultivars that have undergone generations of breeding for yield and size.

Outdoor cultivation offers considerable scheduling flexibility because flowering does not depend on shortening autumn days. Historically, Pitt Bully recommended Northern Hemisphere sowing from roughly March through August, with individual plants completing their life cycle approximately 80 days after germination. Growers in suitable climates can therefore stagger plantings rather than waiting for a single traditional autumn harvest.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Cetme?

Cetme was bred by Pitt Bully from AK-47 crossed with autoflowering ruderalis genetics. The AK-47 parent itself traces to Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan cannabis populations developed into a stable hybrid by Serious Seeds.
Is Cetme an autoflowering strain?
Yes. Cetme was developed specifically as an autoflowering marijuana cultivar. It progresses into flowering according to maturity rather than requiring a conventional 12/12 photoperiod indoors.
How much THC does Cetme have?

Historical breeder specifications place THC at approximately 16–19%. Because the cultivar predates today’s widespread regulated laboratory testing, actual cannabinoid levels should be confirmed from the individual batch whenever contemporary test results are available.
How long does Cetme take to grow?

The complete cycle is approximately 80 days from germination under historical specifications. About 40 days were associated with early development and approximately 40 days with flowering, although environmental conditions can change actual harvest timing.
How big does Cetme grow?

Pitt Bully originally described Cetme as an extremely compact cannabis plant reaching roughly 50 centimeters. Its small stature and automatic flowering behavior make it considerably easier to accommodate in tight spaces than the original AK-47 parent.
Final Thoughts on Cetme

Cetme belongs to an important transitional period in autoflowering cannabis breeding. Rather than beginning with a modern auto line that had already been improved for many generations, Pitt Bully worked from a celebrated photoperiod marijuana strain —AK-47—and used ruderalis genetics to change the plant’s flowering behavior. The resulting marijuana sacrificed some of the size and production of its famous parent but gained a dramatically shorter, simpler growth cycle.

Its heritage is arguably more interesting today because autoflower genetics have changed so much since Cetme appeared. Modern autos can become much larger and considerably more potent, yet Cetme reflects the straightforward philosophy of earlier automatic breeding: take recognizable cannabis genetics, preserve as much of their character as possible, and make them finish without dependence on changing daylight.

For growers interested in compact plants, old-school autoflower history, or AK-47-derived weed, Cetme remains a distinctive cultivar. Its roughly 80-day life cycle, manageable height, predominantly cerebral effect, and classic sweet-citrus-and-spice heritage provide a very different experience from the oversized, dessert-heavy autoflowers that dominate much of the modern seed market.
